cards.text: Elihu, the young man who's been speaking up to Job and his three friends (Job 32:2-6), is STILL going, and now he's talking to Job. He says, "Bear with me a little longer, and I will show you that there is more to be said on God’s behalf." I get it, friend, because I say just one more batch too, and it is NEVER just one more batch.

cards.question: Elihu says he gets his knowledge from afar. Speaking up on God's behalf, he says he will ascribe ___ to his Maker.

cards.text: Elihu says his words are free of falsehood, and that "one perfect in knowledge is with you." Then he gets to his big point: God is mighty, mighty in strength of understanding.

cards.question: Elihu says God is so mighty that He looks down on the weak.

cards.text: Elihu says God doesn't keep the wicked alive, but He grants justice to the afflicted, and He never takes His eyes off the righteous.

cards.question: Elihu says God never takes His eyes off the righteous. Where does God put them?

answers.text: In the house of the LORD

cards.text: But say people end up bound in chains, caught in cords of affliction. Elihu says God tells them their deeds, and how arrogantly they've transgressed.

cards.question: Elihu says God commands people caught in cords of affliction to turn from iniquity. What else does He do?

answers.text: Leaves them to work it out

cards.question: Elihu says people caught in cords of affliction will end their days in prosperity whether they obey God or not.

cards.text: The godless in heart are different, Elihu says: they harbor resentment, and even when God binds them, they don't cry for help. They die in their youth, among the male shrine prostitutes.

cards.question: Elihu says God rescues hurting people. How does He do it?

cards.text: Now Elihu gets personal, saying God drew Job from the jaws of distress to a spacious place, to a table full of richness. Friend, I went from the back of a junk drawer to a whole cookie planet, so I KNOW that kind of spacious.
But now, Elihu says, Job is laden with the judgment due the wicked. Judgment and justice have seized him.

cards.question: When Elihu warns Job to be careful that no one lures him with riches, he also warns him not to let a large bribe lead him astray.
Elihu asks Job about his wealth and all his mighty effort. What's Elihu's point?

answers.text: They can't keep Job from distress
They prove God is still with Job
They should all go to the poor

cards.text: Elihu tells Job not to long for the night, when people vanish from their homes. Then he warns Job about the very thing God commands the afflicted to turn from.

cards.question: Elihu warns Job to be careful not to turn to ___, and he says Job has preferred it to affliction.

cards.text: Now Elihu lifts his eyes higher. God is exalted in His power, he says, so who could appoint His way for Him, or tell Him He's done wrong?

cards.question: Elihu tells Job to remember to ___ God's work, the work men have praised in song.

cards.text: All mankind has seen God's work, Elihu says, and men behold it from afar. ALL mankind, friend, and I can't get everybody in ONE group chat to see ONE message.
God is great, beyond our knowledge, Elihu says, and the number of His years is unsearchable.

cards.question: To show how great God is, Elihu starts with something from the sky. What is it?

cards.text: Then the storm rolls in: who can understand how the clouds spread out, or how the thunder roars from His pavilion? He scatters His lightning around Him and covers the depths of the sea.

cards.question: Right after the lightning, Elihu says, "For by these He judges the nations and provides ___ in abundance."
Elihu says God's lightning just strikes wherever it happens to land.

cards.text: The thunder declares His presence. Even the cattle notice the rising storm.
Elihu says his own heart pounds and leaps from its place. Honestly, SAME, because when my oven door slams I hop a foot in the air, gold base and all.

cards.question: Elihu says to listen closely to the thunder. What does he say the thunder is?

cards.text: God unleashes His lightning to the ends of the earth, then thunders with His majestic voice. He does great things we cannot comprehend, Elihu says.

cards.question: Elihu says God tells the gentle rain to pour out a mighty downpour.
Elihu says God seals up the hand of every man. What reason does Elihu give?

answers.text: So all men may know His work
So no one can fight back

cards.text: The wild animals enter their lairs and settle down in their dens. The tempest comes from its chamber, and the cold blows in on the driving north winds.

cards.question: Elihu says the ice forms and the watery expanses freeze by the breath of ___.

cards.text: He loads the clouds with moisture and scatters His lightning through them. The clouds swirl about at His direction, doing all He commands over the face of all the earth.

cards.question: Whether the storm comes for punishment or for His land, what does Elihu say God does it in?

cards.text: Then Elihu calls Job by name: "Listen to this, O Job; stand still and consider the wonders of God."

cards.question: Elihu asks Job if he knows how God dispatches the clouds or makes the lightning flash. What's Elihu getting at?

answers.text: Job should learn to read the sky
Job brought on the storm himself

cards.text: Elihu even mentions Job's clothes getting hot when the south wind hushes the land, and friend, that's me in a full apron in front of three hot ovens. By noon I'm not baking the cookies, I'm BEING baked.

cards.question: Elihu asks Job if he can spread out the skies like God. Elihu's point is that Job can do it too.
Elihu asks Job to teach them what to say to God. Why does Elihu say they can't draw up their case?

cards.text: Then Elihu asks if God should be told he wants to speak, and if a man would ask to be swallowed up. Friend, that's every meeting where somebody asks for a volunteer, and every arm in the room stays DOWN.
Now Elihu paints one more picture. After the wind sweeps the skies clean, nobody can stare at the bright sun.

cards.question: Right after the picture of the blinding sun, Elihu says God comes out of the north in golden splendor.

cards.text: The Almighty is beyond our reach, Elihu says. "He is exalted in power!"

cards.question: Elihu says that in His justice and great righteousness, God does not ___.
Elihu wraps up by saying men fear God. What reason does he give?

answers.text: He is not partial to the wise in heart
He hides His counsel from all men

cards.text: We'll set this batch on the cooling rack for now, friend, because Job's story isn't over.
